description: Delegated (institution / local) admin permission templates — ADR-0001 §4.
This file is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for what an institution admin may do. It is
read at runtime by app/core/delegated_permissions.py (which renders a template
for one institution slug and enforces it on every /institution-admin/* call)
and applied to Keycloak by scripts/apply_delegated_permissions.py.
Onboarding an institution is therefore: add its slug to `assignments`, run the
script. No clicking in the Keycloak admin console, ever — a console-made grant
is invisible to this file and will be reported by the guardrail audit.
Placeholders: `{slug}` is substituted with the institution's canonical
lowercase slug (ADR-0001 §5.1) when a template is rendered.
Capability vocabulary deliberately mirrors Keycloak's fine-grained admin
permission scopes (view-members / manage-members / manage-membership /
map-roles / view-clients / manage-clients) so that if this platform ever moves
to native FGAP, these templates translate 1:1 instead of being re-invented.
The rule that keeps delegation safe: an institution admin is NEVER granted a
broad admin role, because a broad role talks to Keycloak directly and so
bypasses every fine-grained check expressed below.
Enforced in three places:
1. Config load — a template whose allow-patterns could match a forbidden
role is rejected outright (see also the structural rules in
app/core/delegated_permissions.py: allow-patterns must stay inside the
institution's own namespace).
2. Request time — a caller who holds any forbidden role AND an institution
grant is refused (403) rather than silently over-served.
3. Audit time — scripts/apply_delegated_permissions.py --check-only walks
every institution admin in Keycloak and exits non-zero on a violation,
so it can gate CI / a deployment pipeline.
`realm-management: ["*"]` means NO realm-management client role at all — not
even view-users/query-users, which would let a local admin read the whole
realm and defeat the mandatory institution filter.
`forbidden_realm_roles` lists the platform tiers (admin/super_admin/...) AND
the realm-management role names. The latter are normally CLIENT roles, caught
by the rule below; they are repeated here because a realm role created with
one of those names — or a composite that exposes it — confers the same power
and ADR-0001 §4 names manage-users explicitly.
Which templates are enabled for which institution. `default` applies to any
institution not listed in `by_institution`. Listing an institution with a
shorter list is how you withhold a tier (e.g. an institution that may not
have local auditors).
The full local admin for one institution: manages its people, assigns its
own namespaced roles, and controls which of its own apps its staff may
log in to. Holds no Keycloak admin role — every action is executed by the
wrapper's service account after this template has authorised it.
`roles.deny` withholds inst:{slug}:admin: appointing another local admin
stays a platform-admin action, so delegation cannot become
self-perpetuating. Set it to [] if co-admin appointment should be
delegated to the institution.
People management without app or privilege management: joiner/mover/leaver
for the institution's staff, and the staff role only. Cannot touch client
access, cannot grant hr or admin.
Read-only visibility into the institution's own members and apps. Grants
no write capability at all — useful for internal audit and for service
desks that must look up staff without being able to change anything.
